title: Coordinates, vectors and complex numbers
summary: Place the figure in coordinates, use vectors, complex numbers on the unit circle, or barycentric coordinates, and compute.
key_statements: a,b,c,d \text{ on the unit circle: } ab \parallel cd \iff ab = cd
why: Computation is a guaranteed fallback; choosing the frame that keeps it short is the skill.
references: Chen, Euclidean Geometry in Mathematical Olympiads

title: Geometric inequalities and extremal geometry
summary: Inequalities among lengths, areas and angles of figures: the triangle inequality, Euler's $R \ge 2r$, the isoperimetric inequality, Erdős–Mordell.
why: The isoperimetric inequality is the model for a large part of geometric analysis.

title: Primality testing
summary: The Fermat test fails on Carmichael numbers such as $561$. Miller–Rabin is fast and probabilistic; Agrawal, Kayal and Saxena (2002) gave the first deterministic polynomial-time test.
why: Generating RSA keys requires finding large primes quickly.
references: Crandall & Pomerance, Prime Numbers: A Computational Perspective

prerequisites.title: Fermat's little theorem and Euler's theorem

timeline.title: PRIMES is in P
timeline.who: Manindra Agrawal, Neeraj Kayal, Nitin Saxena

title: RSA and public-key cryptography
summary: Rivest, Shamir and Adleman (1977): publish $n = pq$ and $e$, keep $d = e^{-1} \bmod \varphi(n)$. Encryption is $c = m^e \bmod n$ and decryption $m = c^d \bmod n$. Security rests on the difficulty of factoring $n$.
why: Number theory in daily use, and the reason factoring is studied so intensely.
references: Crandall & Pomerance, Prime Numbers: A Computational Perspective

prerequisites.title: Fermat's little theorem and Euler's theorem

title: Discrete logarithms and Diffie–Hellman
summary: Given a primitive root $g$ modulo $p$ and $h$, find $x$ with $g^x \equiv h$. Diffie and Hellman (1976) used its difficulty for key exchange: Alice sends $g^a$, Bob $g^b$, both compute $g^{ab}$.
why: Baby-step giant-step solves it in about $\sqrt p$ steps; nothing much faster is known for well-chosen groups.
references: Crandall & Pomerance, Prime Numbers: A Computational Perspective

title: The Riemann hypothesis
summary: Every nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ has real part $\tfrac12$. Stated by Riemann in 1859, one of Hilbert's 1900 problems and a Clay Millennium Problem since 2000. Open as of October 2026.
why: It is equivalent to the best possible error term in the prime number theorem.
references: Titchmarsh, The Theory of the Riemann Zeta-Function

prerequisites.title: Nontrivial zeros and the Riemann–von Mangoldt formula

title: The generalized Riemann hypothesis
summary: All nontrivial zeros of every Dirichlet $L$-function lie on $\operatorname{Re}s=\tfrac12$. GRH would give primes in progressions with square-root error and make many algorithms provably fast.

prerequisites.title: Dirichlet L-functions and primes in progressions
